prs.title: chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.407.3
prs.body:
## Problem `posthog-js` is behind the latest release. ## Changes Updates `posthog-js` to 1.407.3 in the workspace catalog, and refreshes the lockfile (pulls in `@posthog/browser-common` 0.2.2). ## How did you test this code? CI: the dependency install runs against the updated lockfile on this branch. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Fully autonomous Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b2116d0438ef43e1aa1c9f51d5dbacbe Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

Updates the workspace catalog and lockfile to use `posthog-js` 1.407.3, including `@posthog/browser-common` 0.2.2. Frozen installation completed with the committed lockfile unchanged, and the frontend SDK contract check confirmed the updated package resolves correctly with its required import paths, declarations, and copied distribution artifacts. ## T-Rex validation blocked The broader frontend build could not proceed past an unrelated HogVM prerequisite because the `parcel` package binary declared by `common/hogvm/typescript` was unavailable. The focused dependency-resolution and frontend-consumption checks completed successfully.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The dependency update is safe to merge based on successful frozen installation and focused frontend SDK consumption checks. No defects were found. The updated SDK passed the same consumer contract exercised against the prior release, including package metadata, frontend imports, declarations, runtime artifacts, and CDN-copy consumption. **Files Needing Attention:** No changed files need follow-up. The unrelated frontend build prerequisite should be repaired separately if a full frontend build is required.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Installed posthog-js@1.407.2 in an isolated pnpm project and ran the authored consumer-contract check successfully. - Performed a frozen-lockfile install and confirmed the lockfile was up to date. - Validated posthog-js@1.407.3 against the consumer-contract check and confirmed it passed across version, main, module, types, seven frontend import paths, 15 required artifacts, and eight required declaration symbols. - Ran the frontend CDN-copy consumption path and verified the required SDK distributions were copied to frontend/dist. - Attempted the narrow frontend build; it was blocked because the HogVM Parcel binary could not be found. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

prs.body:
## Problem We want to know what Garnet Runtime Review evidence a routine dependency update actually produces, so dependency review can lean on recorded runtime behavior rather than the manifest diff alone. ## Changes This branch replays a dependency update taken from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility. The first commit records a baseline dependency install at the branch point; the second commit is the dependency update itself. Dependency transition: ```diff - "@swc/core": "^1.11.4", + "@swc/core": "^1.15.18", ``` ## Evidence comparison pair - Reviewed (head) commit: `607ae123417df1a6816e0351f42b582741076be1` - Compared previous commit from the Runtime Review marker: `d78663fb37b04cc51c4b4199a2dbb5c8b83616a5` - Comparison scope: baseline commit → head, both within this PR (not the PR base branch). ## How did you test this code? No manual testing. Evidence comes from the Garnet Runtime Visibility workflow, which recorded the dependency install on each of the two commits; both runs completed successfully and each produced a Runtime Review comment bound to its commit. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Fully autonomous Devin, running a dependency-update replay measurement. No product code is changed beyond the workflow scoping needed to record the install on this branch. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/36d1756ce54040e1aa448604bd4faafc Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

Updates HogVM’s SWC compiler to 1.15.18 and refreshes the lockfile resolutions used by its TypeScript loader and Jest transformer. The committed lockfile installs successfully, and the updated compiler passes direct transformation, typechecking, and the executable SWC-backed test suites.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No blocking failure remains in the updated HogVM compiler integration. The frozen lockfile install, direct SWC integration smoke checks, HogVM typecheck, and three SWC-backed Jest suites completed successfully with the updated dependency.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Ran the HogVM SWC integration smoke script against the 1.11.4 baseline and the PR 1.15.18 resolution; both runs transformed TypeScript, invoked @swc/jest, and loaded a HogVM TypeScript module through @swc-node/register. - Performed a frozen lockfile install which completed successfully and reported the lockfile up to date. - Executed the HogVM typecheck and the SWC-backed Jest suites; three test suites and 50 tests passed. - The full Jest attempt reached three passing suites and one remaining suite could not run due to an unavailable native re2.node binary after a scripts-disabled install. - Compared manifest and lockfile resolutions and confirmed that HogVM and its integration peers consistently resolve @swc/core 1.15.18. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

prs.title: chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.407.1
prs.body:
## Problem Dependency updates are reviewed from the diff alone, with no view of what the install actually does at runtime. ## Changes This PR replays a historical dependency update taken from this repository's own git history, run under Garnet Runtime Visibility so the dependency install is recorded twice on one PR. The first commit records the baseline install at the branch point; the update commit follows. Evidence comparison pair: - Reviewed / head SHA: `684bbd11dbf4b7b2aada2cb64f33c29f9318e959` - Compared previous SHA (from the Runtime Review marker): `2a700fc1c706a4d7c462a37389470b9f295de888` - Dependency transition: `- posthog-js: ^1.406.2;` `+ posthog-js: ^1.407.1;` - Comparison scope: baseline commit → head within this PR (not immediate-parent-in-history, not PR base branch tip). ## How did you test this code? No product code is exercised. The measurement is the recorded dependency install in CI on this branch; no manual testing was performed. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/65177427738e4e499ea519f2e0b1ea8b Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

This change updates the shared `posthog-js` catalog dependency to 1.407.1, refreshes its resolved PostHog packages, and adds dependency replay documentation. The updated dependency graph installs successfully, but `pnpm-lock.yaml` also upgrades `unlayer-types` from 1.453.0 to 1.457.0 even though no corresponding manifest change requests it. Keep that unrelated resolution unchanged or explicitly include it as part of the dependency update.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The dependency update should not merge as a focused SDK replay until the unrelated installed `unlayer-types` upgrade is removed or explicitly justified. A reproducible installation comparison confirmed that the lockfile change alters the installed dependency graph beyond the requested PostHog JavaScript SDK update. **Files Needing Attention:** `pnpm-lock.yaml` needs attention at the `unlayer-types` package and `react-email-editor` snapshot resolutions.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Generated a P2 finding proof and attached a script to regenerate and install parent and PR dependency graphs, along with the regeneration and installation output. - Generated a proof for a posted P1 finding. - Validated the frontend graph changes by confirming the parent regeneration kept unlayer-types@1.453.0 while the PR regeneration used unlayer-types@1.457.0, and that the frozen graph changes the unlayer-types symlink rather than being lockfile-only. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. General comment **posthog-js-only update includes unrelated installed unlayer-types upgrade** - **Bug** - The PR changes `unlayer-types` from 1.453.0 to 1.457.0 even though the sole manifest change is the posthog-js catalog range. A frozen PR installation resolves `react-email-editor` to `unlayer-types@1.457.0`, while the parent resolves it to 1.453.0. - **Cause** - The committed lockfile refresh includes unrelated resolution movement in addition to the intended posthog-js update. - **Fix** - Regenerate or edit the lockfile so the unrelated `unlayer-types` resolution remains at 1.453.0, or explicitly include and justify the unlayer-types upgrade as part of the dependency update. Ran code and verified through T-Rex
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.407...."](https://github.com/garnet-labs/posthog/commit/684bbd11dbf4b7b2aada2cb64f33c29f9318e959) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=55802678) > Greptile also left **1 inline comment** on this PR.

prs.title: chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.403.0
prs.body:
## Problem We want to know what runtime evidence dependency review actually gets for a routine dependency bump. This PR replays a historical dependency update taken from this repository's own git history, under Garnet Runtime Visibility. ## Changes Dependency transition: `- posthog-js: ^1.402.3;+ posthog-js: ^1.403.0;` Evidence comparison pair: - reviewed/head SHA: `945e390df01556ef72aaadc154991a9960150647` - compared previous SHA (from the Runtime Review marker): `e3093601c46d6153e6ed7e13e129d7a93c410e20` - comparison scope: baseline commit → head, within this PR The baseline commit records a dependency install at the branch point; the update commit records the same install with the new version. ## How did you test this code? No functional testing. The measurement is the recorded dependency install in CI on each commit of this branch. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6080ad23fdb84beb9c54a805e615a0f7 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

This change upgrades the shared `posthog-js` dependency catalog from 1.402.3 to 1.403.0 and refreshes its pnpm lockfile graph, including the related `@posthog/core` and `@posthog/types` resolutions. The potential for a stale or inconsistent catalog/lockfile resolution was disproved: a frozen installation completed successfully across all 113 workspace projects, and `@posthog/replay-shared`, `@posthog/replay-headless`, and `@posthog/frontend` each resolved `posthog-js` 1.403.0.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge: the shared dependency catalog, lockfile, and representative installed consumers consistently use the intended SDK version. No actionable defects remain. The dependency resolution was compared before and after the upgrade, accepted by a frozen workspace installation, and verified from installed consumer workspaces. **Files Needing Attention:** No files need additional attention.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Ran the catalog/importer-resolution checker against the parent and updated commits, and observed that the catalog, lockfile, and three representative importers updated consistently from posthog-js 1.402.3 to 1.403.0. - Ran a frozen workspace installation across all 113 projects, and the lockfile was reported current with installation completing successfully. - Queried the installed dependency resolutions for @posthog/replay-shared, @posthog/replay-headless, and @posthog/frontend; all three resolved to the posthog-js 1.403.0 tarball. - Validated the before-and-after capture showing 1.402.3 before and 1.403.0 after, and confirmed the frozen installation reported the lockfile up to date with the exact resolved package. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

## Problem We want to know what runtime evidence a dependency update produces, so dependency review can lean on recorded behavior rather than diff reading alone. ## Changes This PR replays a historical dependency update taken from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility. The first commit records the baseline dependency install at the branch point; the update commit follows so the two recordings can be compared. Evidence comparison pair: - reviewed/head SHA: `ca54a3eb7f975dd9ca77f70272dc41236b27e0c2` - compared previous SHA (from the Runtime Review marker): `7d2a35e48187fae605911cf128f0defcca1129c6` - dependency transition: `posthog-js 1.399.4 -> 1.399.5` - comparison scope: baseline commit -> head, both within this PR. ## How did you test this code? No application code is exercised. The measurement is the recorded dependency install in CI on each of the two commits. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b3cc8a46e3d24255abe5411c96d20835 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

Updates the workspace-wide `posthog-js` catalog dependency from 1.399.4 to 1.399.5 and refreshes the corresponding lockfile resolutions. A frozen install succeeds, and checked consuming workspaces resolve `posthog-js` 1.399.5 consistently.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No blocking failure remains. The catalog, lockfile importers, and installed workspace resolutions consistently use `posthog-js` 1.399.5.

T-Rex Logs

prs.body:
## Problem Dependency updates are reviewed without any record of what the install actually does at runtime. This branch replays a dependency update taken from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility, so the runtime evidence available for dependency review can be measured. ## Changes Two recorded dependency installs on one PR: - Baseline commit `d578e4c7543c0fa4d8760f6217b19a24d538e7e0` - install at the branch point, no dependency change. - Reviewed head `7a0f5c68d2fb7c8b6d8638a9964687ff675723cc` - the dependency update, `posthog-js: ^1.399.5` to `posthog-js: ^1.400.0`. Evidence comparison pair: head `7a0f5c6` compared against previous `d578e4c`, as recorded in the Runtime Review marker. Comparison scope is baseline commit to head within this PR. ## How did you test this code? No product code changes. Verification is the two recorded dependency installs performed by CI on this PR; both runs completed successfully. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) Measurement branch only; kept as a draft and not intended to merge. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e50167d42f4a4b5cb1bb14042183d7c7 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

The dependency update also replaces the repository’s GitHub Actions workflow set with a single pull-request dependency-install workflow. Because the remaining workflow does not run on pushes or merge-queue events, post-merge validation and merge-queue checks will no longer run.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The change is not safe to merge until required post-merge, merge-queue, release, and security automation is restored. The current workflow configuration leaves one security-impacting failure: repository automation no longer runs for pushes or merge-queue events. **Files Needing Attention:** .github/workflows/garnet-ci.yml

Security Review

 The removed workflow coverage is a CI/CD integrity regression. Release and security automation that previously ran from repository events can no longer execute, reducing protection for merged changes.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Validated a posted P1 finding by running the workflow trigger coverage script and comparing against the baseline, which shows baseline coverage passed and current coverage failed. - Documented a second P1 finding via a review comment with no artifacts attached. - Validated a contract-wide change, showing that removing several workflow triggers left garnet-ci.yml declaring only pull\_request and workflow\_dispatch, and that the mechanical coverage check failed due to missing push and merge\_group; the affected declaration is garnet-ci.yml:9-11. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `.github/workflows/garnet-ci.yml`, line 9-11 ([link](https://github.com/garnet-labs/posthog/blob/7a0f5c68d2fb7c8b6d8638a9964687ff675723cc/.github/workflows/garnet-ci.yml#L9-L11)) **Repository automation trigger coverage is removed** The change deletes the repository’s existing workflow inventory and leaves only this workflow, whose automatic trigger is `pull_request`. It has no `push` or `merge_group` trigger, so post-merge CI and merge-queue validation will no longer run; the removed release and security workflows also cannot execute. Restore the required workflows or provide replacements with the required triggers and check names.
Artifacts
**[Workflow trigger coverage validation script](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/d98761b3-ea48-4350-8369-6bf103e52760)** - Python script executed against both the baseline and current revisions; it parses GitHub Actions YAML and reports workflow event coverage, proving the trigger comparison. **[Baseline workflow trigger coverage passed](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/334a28e6-a27b-4983-9f15-ee574479f434)** - Captured execution of the validation script at \`2518f684c9\`; it found 100 workflows, including 51 push and 24 merge-queue triggers, so baseline coverage passed. **[Current workflow trigger coverage failed](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/d1eb644e-f0e8-48bf-a099-ad2a34a9748f)** - Captured execution of the validation script at current HEAD; it found one workflow with zero push and merge-queue triggers and exited 1, confirming the automation regression.
Ran code and verified through T-Rex 2. General comment **Repository CI, merge-queue, release, and security automation no longer runs after workflow replacement** - **Bug** - The PR removes the previous workflow inventory and leaves only `.github/workflows/garnet-ci.yml`. Its only automatic event is `pull_request`; it has no `push`, `merge_group`, release, or scheduled trigger. Consequently, normal post-merge CI and merge-queue checks will not be created, and removed release/security workflows cannot execute. Security classification: CI/CD integrity and security-control regression. - **Cause** - All prior `.github/workflows` files were deleted in PR scope and the replacement workflow declares only `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` at `.github/workflows/garnet-ci.yml:9-11`. - **Fix** - Restore the required CI, release, and security workflow files, or provide replacement workflows that retain the required `push`, `pull_request`, `merge_group`, release, schedule, and manual trigger coverage and required check names. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

## Problem Dependency review needs runtime evidence, not just a manifest diff. This PR replays a dependency update taken from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility so we can see what the recorded install actually does. ## Changes The branch point records a baseline dependency install; the dependency update commit follows on top, so the two recorded installs can be compared on one PR. No manual testing. Both recorded dependency installs completed in CI and the runtime evidence comment is bound to the head commit above. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Fully autonomous Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/fb0096ab33c34ccd890bf40448d6c757 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

The engineering analytics workspace now explicitly declares its charts dependency and records the corresponding local workspace link in the lockfile. The previously reported installation failure is resolved: a frozen install succeeds and the product workspace resolves `@posthog/quill-charts` to the local charts package.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No blocking failure remains. The affected dependency path was exercised from the engineering analytics workspace. The package declaration and lockfile importer agree, and Node resolves the charts package successfully after a frozen install.

T-Rex Logs

The update was checked with a frozen pnpm installation at both the parent and updated revisions. prs.body:
## Problem Dependency updates land with no runtime evidence about what the install actually executes. ## Changes This PR replays a dependency update taken from this repository's own git history, running the dependency install under Garnet Runtime Visibility so both sides are recorded. Commit 1 records the baseline install at the branch point; commit 2 applies the update. Evidence comparison pair: - reviewed/head SHA: `03448245dd5458901be794b61d54b2d4fb60cd3b` - compared previous SHA (from the Runtime Review marker): `e4635de1a3795f9af8a2c2ba41d3e10be45a0ee2` - dependency transition: `- posthog-js: ^1.400.0;+ posthog-js: ^1.400.1;` - comparison scope: baseline commit to head within this PR ## How did you test this code? Both dependency installs ran in CI on this branch and were recorded; the Runtime Review comment for the head commit compares against the baseline commit above. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/bf620fcb91354c69b5c9243f24a86e89 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

Updates the shared `posthog-js` dependency to 1.400.1 and records the dependency replay context. A frozen-lockfile install completed successfully, and all 24 workspace consumers resolved the updated SDK version consistently. The replay documentation now correctly precedes the dependency-update commit in the current branch history.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No blocking failure remains. The dependency update installs from the frozen lockfile and resolves consistently for every catalog consumer. The current branch history also matches the documented replay sequence.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - I ran a frozen install at baseline and confirmed the lockfile was current and all 24 catalog consumers resolved to posthog-js@1.400.0. - I ran a frozen install on the PR head and verified the lockfile remained current and all 24 catalog consumers resolved to posthog-js@1.400.1, with coherent runtime resolution across workspace consumers. - I executed the dependency replay history validation to verify that HEAD aligns with the replay sequence described in the repository documentation. - I ran the posthog-js-resolution-validation script to confirm the before and after resolution states, showing 24/24 consumers on 1.400.0 before and 1.400.1 after. - I executed the dependency replay history checks before and after, which reported a mismatch before and NO\_MISMATCH with the expected ancestor relationship after the update. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

prs.title: chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.398.0
prs.body:
## Problem Dependency updates are reviewed without evidence of what the install actually does at runtime. This PR replays a historical dependency update from this repository's git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility to measure the runtime evidence dependency review would have had. ## Changes - Commit 1 (`c2b3384`) records a baseline dependency install at the branch point. - Commit 2 (`88d4deb`) applies the dependency update: `- posthog-js: ^1.396.9;+ posthog-js: ^1.398.0;` Evidence comparison pair: reviewed/head SHA `88d4debce1917f7edcc840c227e4d720327ee2cb`, compared previous SHA `c2b3384c5e26adcdcd252cc1b352f9114939c5d6` (from the Runtime Review marker). The comparison scope is baseline-commit → head within this PR, not this PR's base branch → head. ## How did you test this code? No manual testing. The recorded dependency install ran in CI on both commits; evidence comes from the Garnet Runtime Review comment on this PR. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) Prepared by Devin as one unit of a dependency-update replay sweep. Only CI workflow scoping and the recorded dependency update are touched; no product code changes. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7d94caf5259044feb07fef198e516642 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

Updates the shared `posthog-js` workspace catalog and lockfile entries from 1.396.9 to 1.398.0. The potential for an inconsistent or unusable SDK upgrade was disproved: the frontend’s actual SDK copy contract passed with both versions, and the checked frontend and linked workspace consumers resolve to 1.398.0.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge based on the verified SDK consumer contract and consistent workspace resolution. The changed dependency version resolves consistently in the checked workspaces, and the frontend integration successfully copied all required SDK assets with the updated package. **Files Needing Attention:** No files require further attention.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - Ran authored downstream validation commands to test posthog-js 1.396.9 and 1.398.0 in isolated projects, exercising the frontend's real SDK copy contract for array.js, product-tours.js, and conversations.js. - Verified that the installed frontend workspace resolves to posthog-js 1.398.0 and that inspected linked consumers also resolve to 1.398.0. - Generated and inspected the baseline and upgraded validation logs from the authored validation commands to capture the before/after contract results. - The collected evidence shows the upgrade preserves the downstream SDK integration and resolves consistently across the inspected workspaces. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

## Problem We want to know what runtime evidence dependency review actually has to work with when a dependency changes. This PR replays a historical dependency update from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility. ## Changes Dependency transition under measurement: ``` + "uWebSockets.js": "https://codeload.github.com/uNetworking/uWebSockets.js/tar.gz/cfc9a40d8132a34881813cec3d5f8e3a185b3ce3", - "uWebSockets.js": "https://codeload.github.com/uNetworking/uWebSockets.js/tar.gz/cfc9a40d8132a34881813cec3d5f8e3a185b3ce3", + "ultimate-express>uWebSockets.js": "-", ``` Evidence comparison pair: - Reviewed (head) commit: `b8a15359a7d615f5b2d8e8e13ed269c172600872` - Compared previous commit: `d4e26cbf112351bfdf333f5cbf99483082e724c3` - Comparison scope: baseline commit → head within this PR (the baseline commit records the install at the branch point; it is not the PR base commit). ## How did you test this code? No manual testing. The measurement is the recorded dependency install performed by CI on each of the two commits on this branch. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b9ee67ba62884e52a187622b1923c4e7 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

This change makes the pinned `uWebSockets.js` tarball a direct dependency of the Node.js workspace and updates the root override so `ultimate-express` does not introduce its own nested copy. The lockfile also advances `unlayer-types` beneath an unchanged `react-email-editor` dependency, expanding the change beyond the uWebSockets policy update. Revert that unrelated lockfile update before merging. ### T-Rex validation blocked Tool: the dependency comparison and isolated lockfile-reversion check ran, but no artifact-upload mechanism was available to attach its script and output as review evidence.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The intended dependency-policy change is narrowly targeted, but the unrelated `unlayer-types` update should be removed before merge. The final review contains one non-security dependency-scope finding. The manifests do not request an unlayer update, while the lockfile changes its resolved version under an unchanged parent package. **Files Needing Attention:** `pnpm-lock.yaml` needs the `unlayer-types` resolution and the matching `react-email-editor@1.7.11` snapshot reference restored to version 1.440.0.

Ran code and verified through T-Rex

prs.body:
## Problem We want to know what runtime evidence dependency review actually has to work with when a dependency version moves. ## Changes This PR replays a historical dependency update from this repository's own git history under Garnet Runtime Visibility: commit 1 records a baseline dependency install at the branch point, commit 2 applies the update. Evidence comparison pair: | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Reviewed (head) SHA | `c238e67c8e8c17f39912922e17a38ad7cdfe9f38` | | Compared previous SHA (from marker) | `c2f8d91f1777e0aeb996805d96ab0ff993add6f9` | | Dependency transition | `- posthog-js: ^1.392.0;+ posthog-js: ^1.393.0;` | | Comparison scope | baseline commit → head, within this PR | ## How did you test this code? I'm an agent. Both recorded dependency-install runs of the "Garnet Runtime Visibility" workflow completed successfully on this PR, and the runtime review comment was recorded for each of the two commits. No product code is changed. ## Automatic notifications - [ ] Publish to changelog? - [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams? ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) Measurement-only branch pair: the base branch carries just the recorded dependency-install workflow so the two installs are directly comparable. Left open as a draft; nothing here is intended to merge. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e5eeb3d0172b4a2eb42f57e47d6695df Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

The shared `posthog-js` update to 1.393.0 leaves one workspace importer pointing at the removed 1.392.0 lockfile entry. Frozen dependency installation therefore fails before dependencies are installed.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The branch is not ready for frozen dependency installation because `products/posthog_ai` refers to a missing `posthog-js` lockfile entry. A reproduced dependency-install failure remains and requires reconciling the importer with the package and snapshot records. **Files Needing Attention:** pnpm-lock.yaml

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - T-Rex produced a proof for the posted P1 finding and linked it to the corresponding review comment. - T-Rex produced a second proof for the posted P1 finding, anchored to another review comment. - T-Rex validated the frozen-lockfile failure by running the CI reproduction and inspecting the failure output and lockfile context, confirming the missing posthog-js@1.392.0 scenario. - T-Rex documented that the lockfile importer references 1.392.0 while retained entries are 1.393.0, and captured pre-CI command output to illustrate the frozen-lockfile path. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `pnpm-lock.yaml`, line 3799-3801 ([link](https://github.com/garnet-labs/posthog/blob/c238e67c8e8c17f39912922e17a38ad7cdfe9f38/pnpm-lock.yaml#L3799-L3801)) **Frozen install references a missing lockfile entry** The `products/posthog_ai` importer still resolves `posthog-js` to `1.392.0`, but this lockfile retains package and snapshot records only for `posthog-js@1.393.0`. A frozen pnpm install consequently fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY`. Regenerate the lockfile so this importer and its package and snapshot records resolve the same version.
Artifacts
**[Exact requested frozen pnpm install command source](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/292a054d-468a-4d5b-8a46-abed4e515b5f)** - The executable source contains the exact requested frozen, scripts-disabled pnpm install command, takeaway: it documents the initial narrow validation invocation. **[Initial frozen install output without CI](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/abdea316-8d5b-4d47-acb7-55b3286268b4)** - The command output shows pnpm stopped at its no-TTY node\_modules removal protection before lockfile resolution, takeaway: the initial non-CI run did not reach the claimed defect. **[CI frozen pnpm install command source](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/0932d4e0-8bf9-4a27-bf99-d59b7ab3d9ab)** - The executable source sets CI and invokes the same requested frozen, scripts-disabled pnpm install command, takeaway: it is the exact source that reaches lockfile validation. **[Frozen install failure for missing posthog-js 1.392.0](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/48a4c8a6-3a46-42ee-a78a-e83328a4cba9)** - The recorded command exits 1 with ERR\_PNPM\_LOCKFILE\_MISSING\_DEPENDENCY and explicitly names posthog-js@1.392.0, takeaway: the defect is reproduced. **[Numbered PostHog lockfile importer and retained entry context](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/8e4dc772-4b40-4641-9ad6-bc9c7603f85f)** - The captured numbered lockfile slices show the 1.392.0 importer and the only retained 1.393.0 package and snapshot entries, takeaway: the mismatch is directly attributable.
Ran code and verified through T-Rex 2. General comment **Frozen pnpm install references a missing posthog-js lockfile entry** - **Bug** - `products/posthog_ai` resolves `posthog-js` to `1.392.0`, but the lockfile contains package and snapshot records only for `posthog-js@1.393.0`. The requested frozen install deterministically fails before installation with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY`. - **Cause** - The importer resolution was left at `1.392.0` after the corresponding package/snapshot records were removed or updated to `1.393.0`, consistent with pnpm's reported broken-lockfile/merge-conflict condition. - **Fix** - Regenerate or reconcile `pnpm-lock.yaml` so the `products/posthog_ai` importer and the corresponding package and snapshot records reference the same `posthog-js` version, then rerun `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

prs.title: chore(deps): Update posthog-js to 1.396.6
prs.body:
## Problem Dependency updates are reviewed without runtime evidence of what the install actually executes. ## Changes This PR replays a historical dependency update taken from this repository's own git history, under Garnet Runtime Visibility, so the runtime evidence available for dependency review can be evaluated. The baseline install is recorded at the branch point, and the dependency update commit follows on top of it. Evidence comparison pair: - Reviewed (head) commit: `5c7d8ce70f9ea7cff00e5b8b1760114e9bd1e2d3` - Compared previous commit (from the Runtime Review marker): `01742224f5cf32bd4fd6956374556eec69931c6f` - Dependency transition: `- posthog-js: ^1.396.5;+ posthog-js: ^1.396.6;` - Comparison scope: baseline commit → head within this PR (not immediate parent outside the PR). ## How did you test this code? No manual testing. The measurement is the recorded dependency install performed by the Garnet Runtime Visibility workflow on this PR. The baseline run completed successfully; the head run's install step failed partway through a native module build (`lz4` node-gyp), so the head recording covers a partial install. ## Automatic notifications - [ ] Publish to changelog? - [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams? ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) Devin ran this as one unit of a dependency-update replay sweep: create a base branch at the parent commit with only the recorded dependency-install workflow, record a baseline install, then apply the dependency update and record again. No repository skills were invoked. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/90c50f8cbeae4af1b496b3fbea53a863 Requested by: @jadoonf

Greptile Summary

This change updates the workspace `posthog-js` resolution from 1.396.5 to 1.396.6, refreshes the related PostHog package resolutions in the lockfile, and adds a dependency replay note. The reported Quill visual-test compatibility concern was dropped after an executed check exercised the configured matcher and reporter with the Storybook test runner’s Jest 30 runtime. The check loaded Quill’s `jest-image-snapshot` installation, passed the matcher test, and wrote a snapshot successfully, contradicting the predicted failure.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge based on the exercised Storybook visual-test integration path and the absence of remaining findings. The only reported concern was tested through the actual Quill Storybook matcher and reporter configuration under the test runner’s Jest runtime. It completed successfully and did not demonstrate the claimed compatibility problem. **Files Needing Attention:** No files require follow-up. The lockfile peer binding at `pnpm-lock.yaml:1851` was exercised successfully.

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - T-Rex executed the Quill Storybook Jest image snapshot runtime probe script to exercise the image snapshot matcher and the reporter boundary. - The probe ran under Jest 30.0.5 with Quill’s resolved jest-image-snapshot@6.4.0 in a Jest 29 peer context, loaded the configured reporter, passed 1 of 1 test, and wrote a snapshot. - A subsequent run confirmed the same outcome, and the analysis notes that the asserted compatibility consequence is not reproduced; the version split alone is insufficient evidence of a failure. Ran code and verified through T-Rex
